proposals.observation: In the 48-hour quiz window, one session loaded the intro screen and zero sessions advanced past it. The start rate is 0%. The single session came from a Netlify deploy-preview URL, which means it was almost certainly Joel or a collaborator previewing the page, not an ICP visitor. Even so, the intro-load-to-start gap is the highest-friction point in the funnel. If the intro screen does not make the stakes of the quiz concrete and specific within the first few seconds, any real visitor will close the tab before clicking start.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the quiz intro headline and sub-copy. The current text (placeholder shown below as best estimate from deploy-preview context) is almost certainly generic. Replace it with copy that names the specific feeling the ICP arrives with, so a real visitor in that state recognises themselves in the first line and clicks start. The Sultanic test demands something only Joel could write: the gym-bag moment, the unopened tab, the £150k story. One of those anchors belongs in the intro, not in a later email.

You earn well. The numbers should work. So why does opening your banking app still feel like something to get through?

This takes four minutes. At the end, you'll see the specific pattern that's running your money decisions — and what it's actually costing you.

Joel sat on a £150k salary with a gym bag he never unpacked and a tax return he'd had open in a browser tab for six weeks. The pattern was already there. This quiz names it.

proposals.impact: lifts 37.5% open rate closer to Money Vigilance benchmark
proposals.observation: The Money Worship automation has a 37.5% open rate across 16 sends. Money Vigilance sits at 66.67% across 12 sends and Money Avoidance at 52.63% across 19 sends. Money Worship is the clear underperformer, trailing Vigilance by 29 percentage points. Open rate at this stage is almost entirely a subject-line and preview-text problem. The sequence content may be fine; people are not getting past the inbox. A subject-line rewrite is a single-line file change with no risk to the automation logic.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the subject line of email 1 in the Money Worship sequence. The current subject line is likely framed around the label "Money Worship" or a generic benefit promise, which gives the recipient no reason to feel seen. Money Vigilance's higher open rate suggests that sequences opening with a specific, recognisable internal experience outperform those opening with a category name or an aspirational hook. The new subject line should name the exact moment a Money Worship reader will recognise: the thing they bought, the number they told themselves they needed, the quiet discomfort after.
